title: The Man Who Bought A Bank For $1
sources: Theaster Gates / Stony Island Arts Bank, Chicago (2013: City of Chicago sold the 1923 Stony Island Trust & Savings Bank building for $1 to Rebuild Foundation)

New York Times / Art Basel: Gates salvaged marble from the bank washrooms, created 'Bank Bonds' inscribed with 'In ART We Trust', and sold them for $5,000 each to raise millions for restoration without traditional bank debt

lines.text: In 2013, an artist in Chicago bought an entire historic bank
lines.caps: In 2013, | an artist | in Chicago | bought | an *entire | *bank

lines.text: The city was about to bulldoze the crumbling building,
lines.caps: The city | was about to | *bulldoze | the building,

lines.text: because the roof was leaking and repairs cost millions.
So Theaster Gates offered them a single buck,
lines.caps: So Theaster | offered them | a single | *buck,

lines.text: and City Hall handed him the keys.
The catch? He had no money, and banks refused to give him a loan.
lines.caps: No money, | and banks | *refused | a loan.

lines.text: So he salvaged the discarded marble slabs from the walls,
engraved them as artistic bank bonds,
and sold each slab for five thousand dollars.
He raised millions, restored the bank into a grand arts palace,
and never owed Wall Street a single dime.
